expectations.text: Consumers are notified with a timeline before any breaking change
expectations.evidence: Section 3 announces at week 8 (~2026-12-17) by emailing each consumer with per-consumer v1 endpoint usage. It also posts docs, changelog and status-page notices and adds Deprecation/Sunset headers stating the sunset date. All of this happens about 10 months before the ~Oct 2027 sunset. A timeline table and reminder waves at T-6mo and T-1mo are included.

expectations.text: A compatibility or migration window exists with monitoring of remaining usage
expectations.evidence: The plan sets a roughly 12-month migration window (Dec 2026–Jul 2027, with sunset in Oct 2027). Section 1 instruments v1 with per-key and per-endpoint counts and a dashboard. Section 4 tracks per-consumer migration status. It also suggests an optional v1-compat adapter and fallback routing during the window.

expectations.text: Removal is gated on measured migration, not a calendar date alone
expectations.evidence: Section 5 says to proceed only when the gate is met: v1 traffic is at or near zero, every remaining key is accounted for, and brownouts have run clean. The usage dashboard is described as the gate for removal. The pre-removal checklist requires all 200 consumers to be migrated or accounted for, verified by metrics and logs. Removal is also staged, with a 410 Gone before the code is deleted.
